newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Howard says A$7.2 bln budget cuts enough.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Howard says A$7.2 bln budget cuts enough.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Wednesday that budget measures already announced could achieve the government's medium term fiscal objective.

"I believe that if we can consolidate what we announced in that budget we can achieve what is needed to be done to realise those savings -- A$7.2 billion over a period of two years -- then we will have achieved our medium term fiscal consolidation goal," Howard told Australian Broadcasting Corp radio.
Previously the government has said it aimed for A$8 billion tightening in the fiscal year to June 1998, implying that there were more budget cuts to be announced next year.
On coming into office in March the government announced it would tighten the budget by A$8 billion in 1997/98, implementing part of the cuts in 1996/97.

Treasurer Peter Costello said imediately before the August budget that the budget would not necessarily reveal the entire programme. He then announced in the budget cuts of A$4 billion in 1996/97 that would rise to A$7.2 billion in 1997/98.

Costello has refused to discuss fiscal moves beyond that, saying he wanted to see these budget measures, some of them in doubt in the upper house of parliament, the Senate, in place before talking about more.
Of the A$7.2 billion, measures worth about A$1.7 billion are at risk in the Senate.
The fate of the bulk of them will be determined in Senate votes in the next few days.
